name: Better Than a Thousand
label: Revelation
lede: Two guys whose band had gone quiet cut a youth crew demo in Atlanta, handed the mic to Ray Cappo between Shelter tours, and wound up playing America, Europe, Asia and South America without much rehearsal.

eras.title: A demo that got out of hand
eras.text: When Battery went on hiatus, drummer Ken Olden and guitarist Graham Land started writing late-'80s youth crew songs of their own. For a singer they went to the man who had defined the sound, Youth of Today's Ray Cappo, then fronting Shelter. A few songs in an Atlanta studio became a Revelation album within the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Just One · No Echo: Ken Olden
years.h: Two Battery members cut a demo in Atlanta
years.p: Ken Olden and Graham Land record hardcore songs at Issa Diao's studio in Atlanta while [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] sits idle. Diao plays in [[Good Clean Fun|a0e64a50-4480-495b-b98e-2e766b12ea8c]].
years.xp:
Olden told No Echo how it started: "Our other hardcore band, Battery, seemed like it was going to be on a long hiatus, so we started what turned into Better Than a Thousand."

The songs were a demo before they had a singer.

years.cap: Flyer for the band's first show, Safari Club, Washington, D.C., April 26, 1997
years.src: No Echo: Ken Olden · Wikipedia: Ray Cappo
years.h: Ray Cappo takes the mic between Shelter tours
years.p: Olden and Land ask [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]], whom Olden first met at a [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] show in Washington, D.C., in 1988. Jeff Neumann joins on bass.

years.src: Revelation Records: Better Than a Thousand · Revelation Records: pressing history · Wikipedia: Just One · No Echo: Ken Olden
years.h: Just One is done in five days · REV 60
years.p: Cappo records his vocals in two days in a bedroom studio during a Shelter break. Revelation's bio says his voice gets hoarse by the end.
years.xp:
Twelve songs, none longer than 2:40, with artwork by Tom Bejgrowicz. Revelation pressed 2,029 on black and 517 on clear, and Wikipedia says the band built a large following off it.

Olden, looking back, kept the rough edges: "I'd tweak a lot if I could do it all over but I appreciated the raw effort being mostly retained from start to finish."

eras.title: Four continents, then California
eras.text: Better Than a Thousand toured harder than most full-time bands: America, Europe, Asia and South America. The second album was made in Olden's bedroom and bathroom, and when Cappo moved to California the band stopped.

years.h: Value Driven gets made in Ken Olden's bedroom and bathroom
years.p: The second album opens a track with an extract of Gandhi on nonviolence, I'll Not Resist, per Punknews. Olden's own pick for the best song is Demand Independence.
years.xp:
Olden says this was the record where the band stopped winging it: "Value Driven was us realizing we had created something special and making a much more deliberate effort."

Punknews found it more modern and fine-tuned than Youth of Today's approach, and noted it ends on an experimental instrumental, like the debut.

years.cap: A Better Than a Thousand crowd singing along, Pennsylvania, winter 1998
years.h: Four continents on songs too simple to rehearse
years.p: Better Than a Thousand play America, Europe, Asia and South America behind Value Driven. Olden says the songs were simple enough to tour without rehearsing.
years.xp:
Olden puts the draw down to energy and message more than chops: "Most of our shows were packed, and everybody brought all their spirit to the shows."

Footage from the year includes sets in York, Philadelphia, and Szombathely, Hungary, on the European run.

years.h: Self Worth single is the last new release
years.p: It comes out on Grapes of Wrath, and nothing new follows.

years.h: Cappo moves to California, and the band simply ends
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Cappo relocates to California and leaves straight edge. The band breaks up, and he turns toward teaching yoga.

eras.title: Back in print
eras.text: Better Than a Thousand never reunited, but the records kept returning: a Record Store Day repress of Just One, then a deluxe reissue of both albums that Olden remixed himself.

years.h: Revelation presses Just One again for Record Store Day
years.p: 772 copies on opaque red for Record Store Day and 328 on opaque grey.

years.big: "So much more than we ever had imagined."
q: Better Than a Thousand did so much more than we ever had imagined us doing with it
years.src: No Echo: Just One and Value Driven
years.h: End Hits reissues both albums with five bonus songs each
years.p: Ken Olden remixes and remasters Just One and Value Driven and records additional guitar. The CD is limited to 500 copies.
years.xp:
Announced in April 2020, the reissues add five rare songs to each album and a 36-page fanzine, We Must Believe, of unpublished photos and liner notes. Vinyl came with a poster and download code.

Olden on the run overall: "Better Than a Thousand did so much more than we ever had imagined us doing with it."
